summary: This change adds a persisted production/staging release channel. The channel selects the control-plane origin, the session file, and the update repository, and a "Use Staging" menu item switches it and relaunches the app. The coverage gate fails: 80 changed lines are uncovered, including all of the channel-to-config mapping and the menu switch flow. A bad or unreadable channel file also crashes startup, and the user has no way to recover from inside the app.

findings.body: `readConfig` returns `readReleaseChannel`'s error whenever the `release-channel` file has unexpected contents or cannot be read (permissions, EISDIR, a partial write). `main.ts:47-50` then throws at module load. The packaged app crashes before any window or menu exists, so the user cannot switch back from inside the app and must find and delete a hidden file in userData. Before this change, this failure mode did not exist. An auxiliary preference file should not be able to brick startup. Fall back to `production` and surface the problem: log it after the logger exists, or return the read error alongside the config so `main.ts` can log it or show a dialog. Then update the temp tests to match.

No test loads `electron.ts`, `AppUpdates.ts`, `ControlPlaneAuth.ts`, or `main.ts`, so 80 changed lines are uncovered and none is exempt. The behavior that matters is untested: the channel-to-config mapping (staging origin, `staging-control-plane-session` path, `cashew-labs/halo-staging` update repository), the rule that dev and test modes ignore the channel for the origin and for updates, and the update feed URL and `updateSource` built from `config.repository`. The temp test covers only the file read and write helpers.

testRequests.target: packages/config/src/electron.ts readConfig (lines 90-125): mock `electron`'s `app` (isPackaged true/false, getPath, setPath) and HALO_USER_DATA, then assert controlPlaneOrigin, controlPlaneSessionPath, and updates.repository for production with no file, production with a `staging` file, and development with a `staging` file (development origin, updates disabled)
testRequests.rationale: This mapping is the core of the feature: wrong values send users to the wrong deployment or update feed.

testRequests.target: packages/config/src/electron.ts:92: an invalid or unreadable release-channel file must not make config resolution fail (after fixing F1)

apps/electron/src/main/app/AppUpdates.ts:77 and 154-156: with `electron` and `update-electron-app` mocked, assert the darwin feedUrl contains the configured repository and that updateElectronApp receives `{ type: ElectronPublicUpdateService, repo }`
testRequests.rationale: Confirms that updates actually follow the selected channel.

testRequests.target: apps/electron/src/main/main.ts:494-531 switchReleaseChannel: on cancel, the menu is rebuilt and nothing is written; on confirm, the file is written and relaunch/quit is called; on a write error, the error box is shown and there is no relaunch. Use a test, or an exemption with a concrete reason if the main-process module cannot be loaded in vitest
testRequests.rationale: These changed lines are currently uncovered and not exempt.
